options.misconception: The caption names Cleveland, not New York City.
Pittsburgh was Carnegie's steel city, not Rockefeller's base.
Titusville was the site of the first oil well, not Rockefeller's base.

rationales.A: The caption names Cleveland, not New York City.
rationales.B: The caption says Rockefeller built Standard Oil “from his Cleveland base” — Cleveland, Ohio, was where the refining business grew.
rationales.C: Pittsburgh was Carnegie's steel city; the caption puts Rockefeller's base in Cleveland.
rationales.D: Titusville was the site of the first oil well in 1859, not Rockefeller's base.
rationales.general:
Read the caption's words.
1. The portrait shows Rockefeller in 1880, when Standard Oil was the largest refiner.
2. The caption says he built it “from his Cleveland base.”
3. Cleveland is in Ohio, and the caption names no city.
4. Background: Pittsburgh was Carnegie's steel city, not Rockefeller's base.
Remember: a caption's place name is a fact to use.

stimulus.text: John D. Rockefeller, photographed by Napoleon Sarony in 1880. By then he had built Standard Oil into the largest oil-refining business in the country, refining far more oil than any rival, from his Cleveland base.
